# Support agent chat

## Problem Statement

The engine has since changed underneath the client in three ways. `hal-engine-single-terminal-frame` (#148) makes `stream_end` the single terminal frame, sent once per accepted message, after a measured probe found an `INVALID_MESSAGE` answer to an unrelated malformed frame landing between two `entry_delta` frames of a healthy stream. A client that clears `busy` on any `error` frame drops the typing indicator and unlocks the composer mid-answer. `hal-engine-subprotocol-marker` (#150) stops echoing the client's subprotocol offer and selects only the reserved marker `hal.v1`, so a bare-token offer fails the handshake in both `ws` and Chromium and no customer could connect. The engine's error path now commits the last entry before the `error` frame,…

## Tech notes

Out of scope: the engine half - a sibling issue owns `stream_end` as the single terminal frame and the protocol doc inversion, and another owns committing open entries on every terminal path; what the error frame says and when its notice clears - owned by the Danish failure-messages work, this issue only guarantees `state.error` is still set; redefining `ChatErrorInfo.interrupted`, queued as its own task since both this change and the entry-commit fix invalidate its current computation point; suppressing or restyling an advisory error that arrives mid-healthy-stream - today's behavior of rendering it anyway is kept, any change there is a product question for the failure-messages work; reconnect and resume - the close branch's `busy` clearing is unchanged from `044`. Key sour…

Under `139` there is now exactly one terminal signal - `stream_end`, sent exactly once per accepted message, error or not - and that issue explicitly supersedes `044`'s client-side rule and queues this issue as the correct…

# Support agent chat

## Problem Statement

The engine has since changed underneath the client in three ways. `hal-engine-single-terminal-frame` (#148) makes `stream_end` the single terminal frame, sent once per accepted message, after a measured probe found an `INVALID_MESSAGE` answer to an unrelated malformed frame landing between two `entry_delta` frames of a healthy stream. A client that clears `busy` on any `error` frame drops the typing indicator and unlocks the composer mid-answer. `hal-engine-subprotocol-marker` (#150) stops echoing the client's subprotocol offer and selects only the reserved marker `hal.v1`, so a bare-token offer fails the handshake in both `ws` and Chromium and no customer could connect. The engine's error path now commits the last entry before the `error` frame,…

Author: saadahmed95
Date: 2026-09-29T12:15:31Z

Keep the chat busy through an error frame until stream_end or close

HAL Engine 0.3.0 ends every user_message with exactly one stream_end,
errored or not, and can send an unrelated error (an INVALID_MESSAGE

answer. The error branch cleared busy and stopped every streaming
entry, so that frame unlocked the composer and froze the answer
mid-sentence. It now only records the error; stream_end and a close
stay the run's terminators and keep their isStreaming sweep as the
backstop.
